name: ADC0831
full_name: 8-Bit Serial I/O A/D Converter with Single Differential Input
description: 8-bit successive-approximation A/D converter with a serial I/O compliant with TI's MICROWIRE standard for direct interface to COPS-family processors, and easily bit-banged from any microprocessor or shift register. The ADC0831 is the single-channel differential-input member of the ADC0831/2/4/8 family (0832 adds a 2-channel mux, 0834 a 4-channel mux, 0838 an 8-channel mux); it has no address/DI pin because there is nothing to select. Originally a National Semiconductor design, continued by TI (National's ADC family retains the '-N' suffix post-acquisition). Operates ratiometrically from a single 5V supply or with an external VREF to encode a smaller analog span across the full 8 bits; needs no zero or full-scale adjustment.

pins.name: CS
pins.description: chip select, active low; must be low to enable CLK and start/continue a conversion, high tri-states DO

pins.name: VIN(+)
pins.description: noninverting analog input of the differential pair

pins.name: VIN(-)
pins.description: inverting analog input of the differential pair; sets the analog zero/offset for VIN(+)

pins.name: GND
pins.description: ground reference for both analog and digital sections

pins.name: VREF
pins.description: reference voltage input; sets the full-scale (256-code) span. Tie to VCC for ratiometric 0-5V operation, or reduce below VCC to encode a smaller analog span across the full 8 bits

pins.name: DO
pins.description: serial data output, tri-state; shifts out the conversion result MSB-first then LSB-first on CLK falling edges, tri-states when CS goes high

pins.name: CLK
pins.description: external clock input; also times the successive-approximation conversion (10 kHz min to 400 kHz design limit, 40-60% duty cycle)

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: positive supply, 4.5V to 6.3V operating (6.5V absolute max); also the ratiometric reference if VREF is tied to it

extra.input configuration: single differential channel (VIN+/VIN-), no multiplexer or address pin
extra.total unadjusted error: +-1/2 LSB (B-grade, e.g. ADC0831BCN) or +-1 LSB (C-grade, e.g. ADC0831CCN/CCWM/CIWM), tested at VREF=5.00V
extra.conversion time: 32us typ, tC = 8 clock periods (not including CS setup/MUX addressing time) at fCLK=250kHz
extra.clock frequency: 10kHz min to 400kHz design limit; specs given typ at fCLK=250kHz
extra.clock duty cycle: 40% to 60% (clock may be stopped low indefinitely if analog input is stable, or high up to 60us max)
extra.input voltage range: 0V to 5V with single 5V supply; VIN(-) staying within ~50mV of the rails avoids input-protection-diode conduction (needs VCC >= 4.95V for a true full 0-5V span)

typical_application: Low-cost 8-bit data acquisition of a single differential analog channel over a simple CS/CLK/DO serial interface compatible with TI MICROWIRE and easily bit-banged by any microprocessor; typical uses include reading a bridge or pressure sensor differentially, or a ratiometric potentiometer/thermistor front end feeding a COPS or general-purpose MCU.
gotchas: the -N suffix (ADC0831-N/0832-N/0834-N/0838-N) marks TI's continuation of the original National Semiconductor ADC0831 family after the 2011 acquisition; it is not TI's usual NRND marker
ADC0831 has no input mux or DI (address) pin, unlike its siblings ADC0832 (2-ch mux), ADC0834 (4-ch mux), and ADC0838 (8-ch mux) -- it is permanently wired as one differential channel

DO shifts out MSB-first immediately, then re-shifts the same result LSB-first afterward; a receiver expecting only one bit order will misread half the transmission if it doesn't stop clocking after 8 bits
VREF sets the full-scale span (not just a bias): tie to VCC for ratiometric 0-5V operation, or drop it below VCC to encode a smaller analog span across the full 8-bit code

VIN(-) must stay close to GND (within ~50mV) or its internal protection diode conducts and corrupts the conversion; a true 0V-5V single-supply input range requires VCC >= 4.95V to keep enough diode margin

the 6.3-8.5V internal zener/shunt-regulator trick for running from higher supply voltages needs the separate V+ pin, which the PDIP-8/SOIC-8 ADC0831 package does not break out (only VCC) -- that trick applies to the ADC0834-N/0838-N packages that do expose V+
